dossier.architecture: Full-width intake, vertically translating reversible shooter and separate chain hooks.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; underfloor cross-shafts package elevator drives.
subsystems.intake: Omni wheels and printed wedges center notes after experiments with other wheel types.
subsystems.transfer: Shooter aligns with intake for transfer, then retains the note for the selected destination.
subsystems.scoring: Top/bottom shooter on a rotating carriage; intake rollers gently release amp/trap notes.
subsystems.endgame: Linear hook slides hold the chain while the scoring carriage rises to trap height.
subsystems.controls: Two Limelights aim relative to tags; high fixed-pose defensive shot bypasses occluded tag aiming.

versions: Prototype options included side-wheel and windup launchers. Removed wheels in regions not contacting the note to reduce rotating mass.
dossier.analysis: The same reversible carriage handles several destinations, but requires careful alignment and sequencing. Their high defensive shot is an alternate operating mode, not evidence that every normal shot clears a defender.

context_documents.title: 2024-1756 · Omni centering and reoriented transfer need defined staging states
context_documents.body:
# 2024-1756: Omni centering and reoriented transfer need defined staging states

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Omni wheels and printed wedges center the note while allowing lateral motion. The rotating shooter aligns with the intake to receive it; paired sensors detect travel and possession. The same moving assembly uses gentle roller release for amp/trap rather than a high-speed shot.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team identifies lateral freedom as the reason for the omni contact choice. Sensor feedback reduces the driver’s need to see the note and helps avoid acquiring a second piece.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A roller can create useful forward traction while resisting necessary lateral centering. Omni contact addresses that conflict, but the wedges still establish the note’s final alignment. A moving transfer interface adds a temporal constraint: feeding must wait for receiving geometry, then stop at a verified state before reorientation. Gentler release for a confined goal is a separate control mode from speaker firing.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test diagonal entries and sensor disagreement; measure capture/transfer tolerances at the rotating interface and retention during the following motion.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
